Subject: POC capacity planning - reserved GPUs & autoscaling

Hi Jason & Priya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on scope and success criteria. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize proposed evaluation plan, capacity needs, and next steps so we can lock the POC timeline. I attached a short capacity estimate workbook (redwood-poc-capacity-estimate.xlsx) and a proposed MOP (poc-mop-v1.docx).

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Success criteria: (1) <10% tail latency for 128-token generation under 95th percentile; (2) model responses meet a 4/5 quality threshold on your eval set; (3) integration with your inference pipeline completed and serving from your VPC (optional) or Redwood Dedicated.
- Evaluation plan: 2-week ramp, 1-week steady-state evaluation. Week 1: functional tests and model validation. Week 2: scale tests and latency/cost benchmarking with real traffic slices.
- Timeline: Target start week of Oct 12; kickoff docs signed by Oct 8 (DocuSign link to follow).
- Ownership: Marissa (AE) — overall project lead; Rishi (SE) — infra & perf lead; Monica (CS) — onboarding & success; Jason/Priya — Acme product/infra owners.

Capacity ask (initial proposal):
- Reserved GPUs: 4x A10G-equivalent reserved for steady-state (supports ~120 concurrent RPS at 128-token median vector size based on our benchmarks).
- Autoscaling: allow burst to +50% capacity (2 additional on-demand GPUs) for traffic spikes; scale back policy to steady state after 10 minutes of lower load.
- KV/prefix cache: enable prefix caching for hot queries — this reduces per-token cost and lowers p95 by ~20% for repeat queries.

Action items / next steps:
1) Jason/Priya: confirm target start week (Oct 12) and any blackout dates by EOD Oct 5.
2) Acme: share 1-2 representative prompts + small eval set (50 examples) by Oct 5.
3) Rishi/Monica: provide final capacity table and onboarding checklist by Oct 6.
4) Marissa: send DocuSign statement of work + PO template by Oct 6.

Attachments: redwood-poc-capacity-estimate.xlsx, poc-mop-v1.docx

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if useful.

Best,

Hi Jason — answering inline to keep it concrete.

1) Assumptions for 4x A10G estimate:
   - Target concurrency: 120 concurrent requests for 128-token generations.
   - Average tokens per request: 160 (including prompt + expected generation).
   - Batching: continuous batching with 32-request batch size avg during steady traffic; 85% GPU utilization target for cost-efficiency.
   - Model: open-llm-v1 (quantized int8) — if you select a larger model, numbers will shift ~+30-60%.

2) Burst autoscaling latency:
   - For Dedicated: node provisioning + model warmup typically 90–150s depending on region and image cache. We recommend keeping the 2-minute SLA for critical spikes; to hit <2 min consistently we suggest a small warm pool (1 warm GPU) and rapid pre-warming based on traffic prediction — see sheet tab 'Burst strategy'.

3) Telemetry: Dedicated exposes Prometheus-compatible metrics (request latency histograms, token counts, GPU utilization), trace ids for sampling, and per-route cost breakdowns. We can provide a read-only Grafana dashboard and a metrics endpoint to integrate with your SREs.

I'll drop an updated capacity estimate that includes a warm pool option and the burst timing — attaching as updated: redwood-poc-capacity-estimate.xlsx (v2).

- Rishi
